title: Octavia Spencer Monologue
text: Ladies and gentlemen, Octavia Spencer. -...come true to be here. No, no, really. I've spent the last four months of my life at award shows, doing interviews, and walking red carpets. So, this is my first real night out of my Spanx. I'm just kidding. I'm still wearing Spanx. And, by the way, did y'all watch the Oscars? I mean, what was that? How crazy was it that I didn't win? Oh, look, but I mean it when I say it truly is an honor to be nominated, because, for a good part of my career, I pretty much just played nurses. I played a nurse 16 times. I did it so many times that, when I played a maid, they gave me an Oscar. I guess I have what Hollywood calls resting nurse face. For example, I've played nurse that's had it. Nurse that's had it up to here. And nurse that had it so bad this happened. Yeah, she got stabbed bad. So, after all that, it was so wonderful to play a NASA mathematician like I do in hidden figures. Been so kind to me about that when I was a kid, I was like, So many people have been coming up to me saying, I loved Hidden Fences! And I say, no, I was in Hidden Figures. I mean, I get it. I get it. There were three black movies at the Oscars this year. And that's a lot for Americans. So if you're gonna get confused anyway, I thought I might as well make some money off it. That's why I produced Hidden Fence Light. It's the story of three black women who send an introspective gay boy to build a fence on the moon. Great show for you tonight!
